title: Ops SLO Rituals & Decision Lab — 72-Day Playbook (Working Draft)
body:
Purpose

This is a working playbook for running a time-boxed, cross-functional reliability program built around three components: (1) a 72-day plan broken into three 24-day cycles, (2) weekly "Decision Lab" sessions for rapid tradeoff decisions and experiments, and (3) defined SLO taxonomy + error-budget rules tied to rollout gates.

Audience
- Platform engineering (owners)
- Serving runtime engineers
- Observability & telemetry
- Product/feature owners (hosted API, Dedicated, Private)
- Customer-facing teams (support/CS)

High-level goals (why)
- Reduce user-facing latency regressions by 30% for critical generation routes over 72 days.
- Standardize SLO measurement and error-budget policy across 3 product slices (API, Dedicated, Private).
- Build a repeatable cross-team decision ritual to triage, prioritize, and run micro-experiments that reclaim error budget without blocking launches.

Success metrics (what counts)
- P95 latency for /v1/chat completions down from baseline by 30% on targeted routes (24-day sprint metric).
- Error-budget burn rate stabilized within policy threshold after each Decision Lab (<= 1.2x target burn).
- 80% of SLO-related incidents get a one-paragraph remediation plan within 48h and an experiment assigned within 5 working days.

Scope & non-goals
- In-scope: SLO design, telemetry contract, runbook triggers, experiment templates, rollout gates.
- Out-of-scope: long-term infra rewrites, procurement of HW, or full model architecture changes (those are follow-ups).

72-day rhythm (structure)
- Macro: 72 days = 3 cycles x 24 days. Each 24-day cycle = 3 x 8-day squads (planning / rapid iteration / wrap and learn).
- Sprint 1 (days 1-24): Baseline measurement, small-signal remediations, Decision Lab pilot.
- Sprint 2 (days 25-48): Implement 2 medium-impact mitigations (e.g., KV-cache TTL tuning, dynamic batching policy), expand telemetry coverage.
- Sprint 3 (days 49-72): Run A/B for rollout policies, codify runbooks, handoff to steady-state ops.

Weekly cadence (rituals)
- Monday: Signal snapshot (15m) — owners post a 2-line summary in #reliability-digest (p95, error budget burn, top 3 alerts).
- Wednesday: Decision Lab (90m) — cross-functional workshop to triage, prioritize, and assign experiments.
- Friday: Sync & retro (30m) — short update on experiments, blockers, and decisions captured to Confluence.

Decision Lab design (how it runs)
1) Inputs (pre-read by end of Tuesday):
   - Snapshot document: p50/p95/p99, error-budget burn trend (hourly), recent deploys, customer impact notes.
   - Shortlist of candidate interventions (one-line each).
2) Attendees (required): owner, telemetry rep, SRE, product rep, solutions engineer. Optional: oncall rotation.
3) Artifacts produced: decision outcome (accept/reject/defer), assigned experiment owner, expected impact estimate (low/med/high), rollback criteria, measurement plan.
4) Decision heuristics (quick):
   - Priority Score = User Impact * Exposure / Cost-to-try. (Use ordinal buckets: 1-3)
   - If Priority Score >= 6 => green to experiment within 72 hours.
   - If experiment risk = high and impact = med, prefer canary with auto-fallback.

SLO taxonomy (proposal)
- Service SLOs (user-facing): request success rate (>= 99.9%), p95 latency (user-route-specific), model-fallback rate (fallbacks per 1000 requests <= 2).
- Platform SLOs (internal): deployment success, KV cache hit-rate thresholds, inference node restart frequency.
- Observability SLOs: telemetry freshness (metrics delayed less than 5m 99% of the time).

Measurement contracts (what to measure + where)
- Metric name, ownership, collection method, aggregation window, alert thresholds.
- Example (route: /v1/chat):
  - metric: chat_gen_p95_ms | owner: serving-runtime | collection: edge->ingest->prom | window: 5m
  - metric: chat_error_rate | owner: api-gateway | collection: edge | alert: >0.1% for 10m
- All metrics must be linked to a dashboard tile and a lightweight runbook snippet.

Error budget policy (short)
- Error budget period = 30 days for service SLOs.
- Burn states: OK (<=1x burn), Watch (1-2x), Action (>2x)
- If state = Watch => Decision Lab must evaluate remedial experiments within 48h.
- If state = Action => temporary rollout freeze for new non-critical features until burn returns to Watch/OK OR an approved mitigation is in flight.

Experiment templates (repeatable)
- Quick A/B (canary)
  - Hypothesis, segment %, metrics to watch, rollback trigger, owner, duration (48-96h).
- Configuration toggle (e.g., batching window)
  - Safety bounds, expected cost delta, test harness route, measurement spec.
- Capacity spike drill (stress small pool)
  - Synthetic load plan, expected failure mode, experiment owner.

Roles & responsibilities (RACI-style minimal)
- Platform Eng (owners): coordinate Decision Lab, maintain SLO catalog, run central dashboards.
- Observability (telemetry): guarantee metric freshness, maintain instrumentation PR backlog.
- Serving-runtime: implement config changes, measure impact.
- SRE: author runbooks, own incident comms.
- Product: prioritize user-impact and accept tradeoffs.

Oncall & incident handoff notes
- Trigger from metrics -> declare 'SLO incident' if 3 signals cross (p95, error rate, fallback rate) for 10m.
- On-call executes immediate remediation (scale, throttle, failover) and files incident doc.
- Decision Lab reviews incident within next Wednesday slot (if within 72-day window).

Playbook snippets (copyable)
- Immediate scale: add one burst pool in Dedicated for critical routes (owner: infra). Rollback: remove pool if latency not improved in 10m.
- KV cache TTL bump: +30s on hot prefix for 24h can reduce p95 by removing cold-kv reads. Measure: cache hit-rate and p95 over 6h.

Communication plan
- Internal: #reliability-digest for daily snapshots, Decision Lab notes posted to Confluence page under "Decision Lab notes".
- External: CS template for customers impacted by SLO incidents (one-liner cause, ETA, mitigation).

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: Decision Lab becomes a coordination sink (too many low-value requests).
  - Mitigation: pre-filter candidates using Priority Score; cap agenda to 6 items.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps -> poor decisions.
  - Mitigation: telemetry guard rails (freshness checks) and one-page data health checklist before each lab.

Artifacts to deliver by end of 72 days
- SLO catalog (owner, metric mapping, runbook links) — public page.
- 6 experiment reports (short template: hypothesis, outcome, metrics, next steps).
- Decision Lab playbook (this doc matured + templates).
- Handoff checklist for steady-state ops.

Open questions (TODOs)
- Define exact numeric SLO thresholds for non-critical (low-volume) routes — Priya to draft by day 10.
- Agreement on Priority Score weights (Impact:Exposure:Cost) — ask product for guidance in next leadership sync.
- Decide whether error-budget period should align with billing cycle (finance input needed).

Quick action list (first 14 days)
- Day 0-3: baseline dashboards + smoke alerts (who: telemetry).
- Day 3-7: run first Decision Lab (pilot) with 3 candidates (who: platform eng lead).
- Day 7-14: implement 2 low-risk experiments (owners named here).

Notes-to-self / drafting scratch
- Keep Decision Lab to 90m max. Use breakout tracks for deep technical triage.
- Keep artifacts light: 1-paragraph decision, measurement spec, experiment owner.
- Capture a single cause of failure per experiment (avoid mixing config + infra + model changes in the same test).

Appendix: sample Decision Lab outcome (example)\- Candidate: dynamic batching for chat-route A (priority score = 7).
- Outcome: Trial accepted, 10% canary on one region, owner: Marco, measurement: chat_gen_p95_ms, rollback: p95 increase >5% or error rate >0.05% sustained 10m.
- Notes: telemetry gap for model-cache miss metric — add asap.

Document history
- 2026-10-05: initial draft (Aisha).
- 2026-10-12: Decision Lab pilot notes added (Marco, Priya).
- 2026-11-02: telemetry contracts appended (Liam).

---
End of playing draft.

(If you are reading this and want to add a quick item: add to bottom of doc with initials + date. — AR)
